messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan LinkError fitting 8-schools model
parts:
Hi,

One needs to use the same compiler for Python as for PyStan. Perhaps Python was
compiled with g++ and you're using clang (even if it is clang masquerading as
g++).

I've created a stub of a page to collect OS X related problems and solutions here:
https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan/wiki/PyStan-and-OS-X-Mavericks Let us know if
the suggested solution works for you.

Best wishes,

-a

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan LinkError fitting 8-schools model
parts:
Thanks Allen. I had forgotten to mention I'm not on Mavericks but 10.7.5. I was aware of another Stan-users topic with the same info as your link, but I can't make heads or tails of it. I'm sure you're right that various elements of my (i)Python+packages weren't compiled with the same compiler.

I've since updated all my fink packages to avoid obsolete dependencies, but still have the same LinkError. I also had failed tests from numpy.test() and scipy.test() - see underneath dashed line below. I saw this post https://github.com/scipy/scipy/issues/3194 and wonder if I really need to uninstall all my Python packages and rebuild by forcing the same compiler. I'm a little reluctant because it takes a full day for such an immense task. Suggestions? Much appreciated.

-G

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan LinkError fitting 8-schools model
parts:
Looking for folks encountering similar problems with Numpy and Scipy is a good
strategy for finding solutions for this kind of issue.

It seems like paying attention to compiler consistency on OS X has worked well
for people. For example, if one is going to use clang then make sure everything
is using clang.

If it helps, it's possible to identify the compiler used to compile Python just
by launching it. If you type "python" in the terminal the second line will tell
you the precise version of the compiler that was used.

Good luck!

-a
